## State-request queue, game+5D8h

The queue is an MSVC `std::deque<int>`. The producer 004d3ed0 allocates a block with a 10h-byte
`malloc` at 004d3f13 and the drain indexes it as `map[off / 4][off % 4]`, so `DEQUESIZ` is
`10h / sizeof(int)` = 4. Fields relative to game+5D8h:

| Offset | Field |
| --- | --- |
| +0h (game+5D8h) | allocator slot, untouched by push_back and pop_front |
| +4h (game+5DCh) | block map, `int**`; a null slot is an unallocated block |
| +8h (game+5E0h) | block count |
| +Ch (game+5E4h) | head offset, in elements |
| +10h (game+5E8h) | element count |

Block index for an offset: `off / 4`, minus the block count once when it is not smaller
(004e4486 and 004d3eff). One subtraction suffices because neither caller lets the offset reach
two map lengths.

`enqueue` (004d3ed0, `RET 4`) takes a **pointer** to the value (004d3f35 loads through it), so
call sites that look like they push a literal are pushing the address of a stack slot. It grows
when `(head + count) % 4 == 0` and the block count is not greater than `(count + 4) / 4`, and
allocates the target block lazily. The existing ledger record for 004d3ed0 describes the element
as 10h bytes; 10h is the block size and the element is a 4-byte `int`. That address is outside
this packet's lease, so the correction is recorded here rather than applied.

`grow` (004d20d0) enlarges the map by `max(count, max(block_count / 2, 8))` and rotates the
blocks so the sequence starting at the head block stays contiguous, leaving the new slots behind
it. 004d2211 adds only to the block count: **the head offset is not adjusted**, unlike the usual
`_Growmap`. Both native copy branches (004d216d and 004d21a7) produce the same rotation, which

doc_excerpts.text:
`singleton_lifetime_allocate({kind, native_bytes, host_bytes})` returns raw,
uninitialized `malloc(host_bytes)` storage. On failure it uses the actual host
CRT `_callnewh(host_bytes)` retry protocol and throws `std::bad_alloc` if declined.
`singleton_lifetime_free` uses matching `free`. The size adaptation is explicit:
native manager 14h becomes the C++ manager size, native tracked section 1Ch
becomes the lock plus projection metadata, and each pointer remains four bytes.
`native_bytes` and `kind` describe the caller's allocation boundary; they do not
select a second heap or initialize bytes. This helper can allocate the particle
clock while retaining its native +18h preimage.

`NativeLegacySboStringStorage` is statically checked for MSVC Win32: preserved
word at `+0`, a 16-byte union at `+4`, unsigned length at `+14h`, unsigned
capacity at `+18h`, and total size `1Ch`. Capacity below 16 selects inline bytes;
otherwise the first union word is the heap pointer. These routines never alter
the leading word. Primary integration removed the convenience member defaults:
placement construction without parentheses performs no writes, so embedding
this storage in an exception owner preserves its unwritten prefix. Callers must
explicitly establish the native empty fields before first use. There is no
automatic destructor, copy constructor, or
independent owner token in this raw storage type.

# Application object evidence scope correction

The particle startup/header receipts retained 70 application objects. Root independently reconciled the current `bsp_game.vcxproj`, `Cl.items.tlog` and Release object directory: all three contain 80 objects. The earlier `complete_App_objects` fields therefore describe a reviewed subset, not the entire application census. Their 70 before/after byte comparisons remain valid; the other ten receive no unchanged-byte credit. This also qualifies the locale review's reference to those application records.

The ten missing before images are `game_native_entity_registry_process`, `game_native_game_application_frame`, `game_native_game_tables`, `game_native_player_profile_context`, `gameplay_loose_ends_2`, `hit_hull_segment`, `narrowphase_unit_part_shape`, `ship_sub_entity_list`, `unit_message_arms` and `unit_neighbour_fields` (all `.obj`). Their complete current bytes are captured alongside the other 70. Current project membership does not reconstruct their missing before bytes.

The independent census confirms all 70 previously retained after objects still match their before images and current objects. The accepted Core/executable/map/test-log artifact pins remain exact. Complete Core archive and seven-consumer code comparison claims are unaffected. No rebuild, additional test or runtime run was needed for this metadata correction.

The typed-view primary publication now states the subset explicitly. Original raw receipts stay immutable; this report controls interpretation of their historical field names. Evidence: `reports/cc12_particle_model_app_census_scope_correction.json`; Root receipt `local/cc12_particle_App_census_scope/Root_App_scope.json` is 69,560 bytes, SHA-256 `653c2f87a55e9d710232c049c27da1c55d9407bf05515722c125bbb28af5b341`.
